video_caption: The video segment displays a computer screen showing the OpenStax website, specifically the page for the "Astronomy 2e" textbook. Initially, the "Book details" tab is selected, presenting a summary of the textbook and options under "Get the book," such as "Table of contents," "View online," "Download a PDF," and "Order a print copy." The top navigation bar includes links like "Bookstores," "Subjects," and a "RICE" logo. At 0:28, the mouse cursor moves to and clicks the "Subjects" dropdown, revealing a list of academic areas. The cursor then selects "Science," leading to a new page at `openstax.org/subjects/science` that displays a grid of various science textbooks, including "Anatomy & Physiology 2e," "Astronomy 2e," and "Biology 2e." A banner on this page reads, "Peer-reviewed. Openly licensed. 100% free." The mouse cursor then navigates to and clicks the "Astronomy 2e" book cover in the grid, which transitions the view back to the original "Astronomy 2e" book details page at 0:37, identical to the initial screen.

The video segment begins by showcasing a web browser, likely Google Chrome, displaying the OpenStax website for "Astronomy 2e". The primary tab is labeled "Ch 1 Introduction - Astronomy" (Chapter 1 Introduction - Astronomy) and the URL "openstax.org/books/astronomy-2e/pages/1-introduction" is visible. The initial screen presents "Book details," "Instructor resources," and "Student resources" tabs, with "Book details" being active. On the left side, under "Get the book," a white cursor clicks on "View online," which is highlighted in blue, while other options like "Table of contents," "Download a PDF," and "Order a print copy" are also present. The bottom left of the screen briefly shows "Waiting for pi.dot.com..." Upon clicking, the page transitions to an online reader for the "Astronomy 2e" textbook. The layout changes, now featuring a left sidebar with "Contents" (active) and "Highlights." The "Table of contents" lists sections such as "Preface," "Science and the Universe: A Brief Tour," "1.1 The Nature of Astronomy," "1.2 The Nature of Science," "1.3 The Laws of Nature," "1.4 Numbers in Astronomy," "1.5 Consequences of Light Travel Time," "1.6 A Tour of the Universe," "1.7 The Universe on the Large Scale," "1.8 The Universe of the Very Small," "1.9 A Conclusion and a Beginning," and "For Further Exploration," followed by "2 Observing the Sky: The Birth of Astronomy." The main content area displays a large, vibrant image of two interacting spiral galaxies, labeled "Figure 1.1 Distant Galaxies." A caption explains that these galaxies are so far away their light takes hundreds of millions of years to reach Earth, and they were photographed by the Hubble Space Telescope. A "Search this book" bar is located above the image. Throughout the segment, the system clock in the bottom right corner shows the date "06/23/2023" and transitions from "2:44 PM" to "2:45 PM." The speaker's voice notes that an account is not required to view the book.

The video displays a web browser on a desktop, showing an OpenStax digital textbook titled "Astronomy 2e - Introduction." The user is logged in, and a dropdown menu shows "Account Profile" and "Log out." The main content area of the page presents the "Introduction" section of the book, which includes text and an image of a planet. The left sidebar contains "Contents" and "Highlights" tabs. The user selects a paragraph of text: "We invite you to come along on a series of voyages to explore the universe as astronomers understand it today. Beyond Earth are vast and magnificent realms full of objects that have no counterpart on our home planet. Nevertheless, we hope to show you that the evolution of the universe has been directly responsible for your presence on Earth today." A small popup appears, offering several color options (yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, grey/white) for highlighting and a text field labeled "Add a note..." The user selects the blue color, and the text is highlighted in light blue. They then type "Cool" into the note field and click "Save." A small speech bubble icon appears next to the highlighted text. Next, the user clicks the "Highlights" tab on the left sidebar, which opens a modal window titled "My Highlights and Notes." This window displays the previously highlighted blue text and the note "Cool" beneath it, categorized under "1 Science and the Universe: A Brief Tour." There are filter options for "Chapter" and "Color" (showing "1 Science..." and "Blue" selected respectively) and a "Print" button. The user closes this modal window, returning to the main textbook view.

The video demonstrates how to use the search function on an educational website for an "Astronomy 2e" textbook. Initially, the user is on the "Introduction" page, which displays a table of contents on the left and introductory text and an image of a planet on the right. A search bar labeled "Search this book" is visible at the top. The user types "solar flare" into the search bar and clicks the magnifying glass icon. The page then transitions to "15.3 Solar Activity Above the Photosphere," displaying search results on the left sidebar. This sidebar shows "1 key term result and 30 search results for 'solar flare'" (1 key term result and 30 search results for 'solar flare'), including "Related key terms" and "Chapter results." The main content area now features text discussing "Flares and Coronal Mass Ejections," with the term "solar flare" highlighted in yellow and orange, along with a large image of the sun showing a solar flare. The user scrolls down the search results sidebar, revealing more instances of "solar flare" within various sections. Finally, the user clicks on a search result leading to "15.4 Space Weather." The page content updates to this new section, and the term "solar flare" is highlighted in yellow within the text, indicating its presence on the new page.

The video displays a laptop screen showing a web browser with an OpenStax Astronomy 2e textbook. On the left side, a table of contents is visible. Initially, the section "15.4 Space Weather" is highlighted in the table of contents. At 0:08, the user clicks on "15 The Sun: A Garden-Variety Star," which expands to show its subsections. The user then clicks on "Thinking Ahead" (the introduction to Chapter 15) at 0:14, causing the main content area to display this section, including a large image of the Sun. After scrolling down the "Thinking Ahead" page, the user clicks the "Next" button at 0:20, transitioning to "15.1 The Structure and Composition of the Sun." This new page begins with "LEARNING OBJECTIVES," followed by detailed text, a table titled "Characteristics of the Sun," various figures of the Sun (including a comparison with Earth, sunspots, and a labeled diagram of the Sun's layers like "Corona," "Photosphere," "Sunspot," "Chromosphere," "Convection zone," and "Radiative zone"), and "LINK TO LEARNING" sections with embedded video links. The user scrolls through this detailed content, which also includes a graph showing "Temperature in Solar Atmosphere (km)" versus "Height in Solar Atmosphere (km)." At 0:59, the user again clicks "Next," leading to the "15.2 The Solar Cycle" section, which also starts with "LEARNING OBJECTIVES."

The video displays a computer screen showing a web browser with multiple tabs open, focused on an "OpenStax" online textbook titled "Astronomy 2e." The current page is "Ch 15 Key Terms," as indicated by the URL and page title. On the left side, a "Table of contents" sidebar is visible, with Chapter 15, "The Sun: A Garden-Variety Star," expanded. Under Chapter 15, "Key Terms" is highlighted. The main content area lists various astronomical terms like "photosphere," "plasma," "prominence," and "solar flare," each with a brief definition. A search bar labeled "Search this book" is at the top of the content area. At the 0:34 mark, a cursor hovers over and clicks on the "Summary" link in the left sidebar, causing the main content area to change. The page now displays the "Summary" for Chapter 15, with sections like "15.1 The Structure and Composition of the Sun" and "15.2 The Solar Cycle" providing detailed textual summaries. The bottom right corner of the screen shows the date "06/23/2023."

The video displays a computer screen showing a web browser with the OpenStax Astronomy 2e textbook open to "Ch 15 For Further Exploration." The left side features a "Table of contents," initially focused on Chapter 15, showing sub-sections like "15.1 The Structure and Composition of the Sun" and "15.4 Space Weather," followed by "Key Terms," "Summary," "For Further Exploration," "Collaborative Group Activities," and "Exercises." The right pane displays "Articles," "Websites," and "Apps" sections. The speaker highlights "Collaborative Group Activities," which the user clicks, causing the right pane to display the "Collaborative Group Activities" content. Next, the user clicks "Exercises," revealing sub-sections: "Review Questions," "Thought Questions," and "Figuring for Yourself." The user clicks on each of these in turn, and the main content area on the right updates to show "Review Questions," "Thought Questions," and "Figuring for Yourself," respectively. The user then clicks the 'X' button next to "Table of contents" to close it, then clicks the "Contents" button again to reopen it, and scrolls up, showing chapters from "1. Science and the Universe: A Brief Tour" onwards.

The video opens displaying a webpage for "Astronomy 2e" from openstax.org, showing a table of contents on the left and a chapter titled "Figuring for Yourself" on the right, with the speaker discussing accessing the textbook. The screen then transitions to the book's main page on openstax.org, showing "Astronomy 2e" at the top and a summary of the book. Below "Get the book" on the left, the cursor clicks "Download a PDF." A pop-up appears briefly stating "Downloading..." before changing to "Your PDF is ready," showing an image of a person studying, and offering options to "Give today" or "Send a thank you note," with a "Go to your file" button at the bottom. The user clicks "Go to your file," which initiates loading of a PDF. The screen then fully loads to display the cover of the "Astronomy" textbook, which is teal with large white text "Astro- nomy" and the OpenStax logo, along with a typical PDF viewer toolbar on the left.

The video opens displaying a light blue screen with the white text "Astro-nomy" in large font, with the "openstax" logo in white at the top right. The speaker discusses the legal rights to keep the file after the course. The screen then scrolls down to reveal a white page with black text listing "SENIOR CONTRIBUTING AUTHORS," including "ANDREW FRAWKNOL," "DAVID MORRISON," and "SIDNEY C. WOLFF," each with their respective affiliations (e.g., "FROHM INSTITUTE, UNIVERSITY OF SAN FRANCISCO"). Another scroll shows a page detailing copyright information and publication details for "Rice University" and "OpenStax," including ISBNs for hardcover, paperback, and digital versions. This is followed by an advertisement for "openstax" with the slogan "Study where you want, what you want, when you want." (Study where you want, what you want, when you want.) and an illustration of a laptop showing the online textbook interface. The screen scrolls again to display the Table of Contents, showing chapter headings like "1. The Nature of Astronomy," "2. Observing the Sky: The Birth of Astronomy," and "3. Orbits and Gravity," with sub-sections and page numbers. The speaker highlights the table of contents. Finally, the speaker clicks on "2.2 Ancient Astronomy" (page 46), and the screen immediately transitions to that specific page, displaying the heading "2.2 Ancient Astronomy," followed by "Learning Objectives" and several paragraphs of text about ancient astronomy.

The video displays a screen recording of a computer desktop. In the center, a web browser shows a PDF document titled "Astronomy-2e-WEB_6qnoak." The document is open to a chapter (22) on "Ancient Astronomy," and the mouse cursor is highlighting a blue hyperlink within the text, which reads: "This website about objects in the sky (https://openstax.org/c/theuniverse) allows users to construct a detailed sky map showing the location and information about the Sun, Moon, planets, stars, constellations, and even satellites orbiting Earth. Begin by setting your observing location using the option in the menu in the upper right corner of the screen. An excellent website called figures in the sky (https://openstax.org/f/documents) shows the constellation figures imagined by cultures around the world." The speaker explains that some links in the book lead to external websites (requiring an internet connection), while others navigate to different sections within the book. The screen then quickly transitions to "Earth, Moon, and Sky," which is chapter 4 of the same textbook, illustrating an internal link.

The video opens with a screen displaying a PDF document titled "Astronomy-2e-WEB_6qnoak" in a web browser. The document shows a chapter titled "Earth, Moon, and Sky" with a table of contents. On the right side of the screen, a search bar appears after the user presses "Control + F." The user then types "solar flare" into the search bar. The document then scrolls to Chapter 15, "The Sun: A Garden/Variety Star," and the search results indicate "1 of 19." As the user presses the "next" button, the document scrolls further, highlighting instances of "solar flare" in the text, showing various images of the sun and related tables like "Characteristics of the Sun" and "The Abundance of Elements in the Sun." The search results update to "2 of 19" when a specific section on "Flares and Coronal Mass Ejections" is shown, where "solar flare" is prominently highlighted in red within the text. The speaker explains the search functionality within the PDF, noting that it finds exact matches, unlike the online version which might offer partial matches.

The video begins showing a digital document, likely a PDF, open in a web browser, displaying images of the sun and accompanying text. Browser tabs at the top include "Free Astronomy Book for Down" and "Astronomy-2e-WEB_topicals.pdf," with a "Tools" sidebar on the left. The mouse cursor navigates the PDF briefly before the screen transitions to a website for "Astronomy 2e." The website features a turquoise header with the book's title and navigation tabs: "Book details," "Instructor resources," and "Student resources," with "Book details" currently selected. On the left, under "Get the book," options like "Table of contents," "View online," "Download a PDF," and "Order a print copy" are visible, with the mouse cursor hovering over "Order a print copy." The right side of the screen provides a "Summary" of the book, which describes it as "written in clear non-technical language, with the occasional touch of humor and a wide range of clarifying illustrations."
